analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/qwen-mtp-concurrent-decode.md, lines 1-5) and a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1369-1381). No executable source, auth, crypto, attestation, or protocol code changed in the supplied evidence. The text describes a Qwen MTP decode change. While more than one request decodes, rows run as ordinary chained decode with no policy top-two and no extra readback. The target forward also returns hidden rows, which are appended to the assistant history in step order. The final prompt row's hidden state seeds the first speculative round. Two new env rollback switches are added: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. I found no security regression visible from these docs. Rollback env vars are provider-process-local and do not obviously touch the attestation, coordinator trust boundary, or A-001 plaintext exposure. The real implementation (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory, CBv2MTPConfig) was not supplied, so I cannot verify the following. First, per-request isolation of assistant history and carry under chained concurrent decode (cross-request leakage of hidden state, T-028/T-041 classes). Second, cancellation handling and carry cleanup when a successor step is in flight (T-010). Third, whether the prefill carry interacts safely with SSD prefix-cache checkpoints or restores (T-041, CBv2MTPPrefixCheckpointCoding). Fourth, whether the env switches could be abused by a local operator; the operator is already trusted-adversarial under T-013/T-014 and this is not a new boundary. These are unverified contracts for the code-level review, not findings. needs_deeper_review is true only because the implementing Swift code is outside this batch.
